title: Journey - Five Days of Peace - Day 1: Name your worries

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Peace. <short pause> This is day one, Name Your Worries. <short pause> Over these five days, we'll learn five small steps, each with a few words to say. <short pause> Together they'll become a way back to peace... one you can use in less than a minute, wherever worry finds you.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: For now, just arrive. <short pause> Let whatever is beneath you take your weight. <short pause> Let your breath move at its own speed. <short pause> You don't have to calm down before we start. <short pause> Worried is a perfectly good way to come to God.

Worry often behaves like a message we can't stop rereading. <short pause> We fold it up and put it away. <short pause> A few minutes later, we take it out again. <short pause> We study every line for what it might mean. <short pause> And the more privately we read it, the larger the words become.

A king named Hezekiah once received a letter like that. <short pause> A great army had swept through his country, and now it threatened Jerusalem. <short pause> The letter said, in effect, don't imagine that your God can save you. <short pause> Every frightening sentence was written down, in ink. <short pause> And here is what he did with it, in Second Kings, chapter nineteen, verse fourteen.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: And Hezekiah received the letter of the hand of the messengers, and read it: and Hezekiah went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Did you see what he did? <short pause> He didn't tear it up. <short pause> He didn't pretend it was good news. <short pause> He carried the whole thing into God's presence, and he smoothed it out flat... <short pause> as if to say, You read it, Lord. <short pause> Read what I have been reading.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: So if your worry were a letter, what would it say? <short pause> Give it a first line. <short pause> Dear me... you are going to lose your job. <short pause> Or, the results will be bad. <short pause> Or, they are never coming back. <short pause> Let it use its real words, short and plain. <short pause> There's no need to make them sound faithful.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now picture a wide wooden table, and God on the other side of it. <short pause> Take the letter out. <short pause> Unfold it, one crease at a time. <short pause> Smooth down the corners with your hands. <short pause> Then turn it around, so that the words are facing Him... <short pause> and you don't have to be the only one reading them.

parts.style: tender reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: If any line in your letter describes real danger, spreading it before God can include showing it to someone who can help. <short pause> And if worry ever tells you to harm yourself, please don't stay alone with those words. <short pause> Call your local emergency number, or a crisis line, or a person who can come to you. <short pause> Hezekiah sent for help, too.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Here is the first of our five steps. <short pause> If you can, turn your hands over, palms up, like a page laid open. <short pause> And say these three words to God. <short pause> Here it is. <short pause> Once more, with your palms open. <short pause> Here it is.

parts.style: prayerful, slow, soft but clearly spoken
parts.text: Let's pray. <short pause> Lord, You know how to read. <short pause> Read what frightens me. <short pause> Read the lines I have added myself, and the lines that are true. <short pause> I spread all of it out before You, and I won't hide the worst sentence. <short pause> Bow down Your ear, and hear me. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: warm, steady, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: When worry brings out its letter again today, don't read it by yourself. <short pause> Turn your palms up, wherever they are, and show Him the page. <short pause> Here it is. <short pause> That is all day one asks of you. <short pause> Go gently.
